newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-RONALDO AND SUKER TAKE CENTRE STAGE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-RONALDO AND SUKER TAKE CENTRE STAGE.

text.p: Spanish fans looking to portray the Real Madrid-Barcelona clash as a personal battle need look no further than the rivalry between Real's Davor Suker and young Barcelona striker Ronaldo.
The Brazilian and Croatian aces, who lead the Spanish goalscoring tables with 13 and 12 goals respectively, have grabbed centre stage ahead of Saturday's big clash.
Both men have shone in a season in which their multi-billion peseta team mates have often failed to impress.

And Ronaldo has upped the stakes by betting one million pesetas ($7,600) on the result with close friend and compatriot Roberto Carlos, the Real defender who may be given the unenviable job of marking him.
The loser will choose a charity to benefit from the money, but that will be scant consolation after a game which is attracting an interest unusual even for Real-Barcelona clashes.
The main reason for the attention lies in the massive amounts invested in players by both clubs over the close season.
One newspaper added up the amount another club would have to pay to free both first team squads from their contracts. The total was 62 billion pesetas ($473 million).
Barcelona's main close-season investment was in Ronaldo, but club officials are already having to rewrite the Brazilian's contract to ward off a barrage of offers from foreign clubs.
A string of scintillating individual goals have seen Ronaldo's asking price sky-rocket from the 2.5 billion pesetas ($19.1 million) paid for him over the summer.
Barcelona shirts emblazoned with Ronaldo's name, and the trademark winged glide with which the striker celebrates his goals are appearing in playgrounds all over Spain.

Few Real fans would admit it, but the presence of Ronaldo is undoubtedly responsible for the expectation surrounding the game, and with it the queues outside the ticket booths of the Santiago Bernabeu stadium.
But the home supporters, some of whom will have been waiting for over three days by the time the first tickets go on sale on Thursday evening, have their own Ronaldo to trust in.
"We're going to win 3-0, with a hat-trick from Suker," one fan told a television crew.
A thousand-strong group of supporters at the Real training ground asked Suker and Balkan striker-partner Predrag Mijatovic for a repeat of the 5-0 drubbing that Real handed Barcelona in 1995.
After five years at Sevilla, Davor Suker is widely admired in the Spanish game, but was virtually unknown on the international circuit until the Euro 96 tournament in England.

The Croatian shone in that competition and has continued to come up with the goods since moving to Madrid from Sevilla. Despite a curious one-sided style -- Suker is very much left-footed -- he takes on men with ease and finishes with a powerful shot.
And he knows exactly what it's like to score against Barcelona.
Suker knocked in the winning goal for Sevilla in Barcelona's Nou Camp stadium two years ago and scored with a superb free-kick in a UEFA Cup clash between the two sides last season.

Barcelona coach Bobby Robson is fully aware of the danger posed by the man known to fans as 'Sukerman'. The former England manager has been holding special training sessions for defenders behind closed doors ahead of what he described as "the most important game in the world."
